engine.name: JuMBO tribunal
rules: A JWST/NIRSpec background classification wins over photometric masses.
A spectral type that implies mass ≫ 13 MJup at ONC age means the system is not a JuMBO, even if it is a cluster member.
Pearson masses are conditional: they assume the source is a 1 Myr member at 390 pc.
Photometry-only systems remain unconfirmed. High AV and wide separation lower the planetary-binary score; tight, lightly reddened pairs raise it.
This engine does not discover JuMBOs. It assembles public evidence.

sources.title: Jupiter Mass Binary Objects in the Trapezium Cluster
Independent NIRCam analysis of ONC JuMBO candidates
JWST spectra of brown dwarf candidates in the Orion Nebula Cluster
Radio counterpart and proper-motion limit for JuMBO 24

priorsNote: Luhman (2025) classified seven JuMBO components observed with JWST/NIRSpec (program 2770) as background stars: they lack the H2O bands of young brown dwarfs. Three are named in the text (6NW, 10SE, 11NW). Four further IDs appear only in Figure 1 of that paper, so this engine marks the named three as spectroscopic background and the remaining systems as photometry-only.

chanceAlignment.note: If 540 planetary-mass candidates are sprinkled at random over the 11×7.5 arcmin mosaic, Pearson & McCaughrean expect 3.1 chance pairs inside 1 arcsec. This system's separation is 0.92". p(a random PMO has a neighbor this close) ≈ 0.0048.

verdict.label: unconfirmed
reasons: No published NIRSpec classification for this system in the text of Luhman (2025). Pearson masses assume a 1 Myr ONC member at 390 pc — they are not independent confirmation.
Mean AV ≈ 5.3. Low extinction makes a background-giant impersonation harder, though still not a spectrum.
Projected separation 357.7 au is at the wide end of the 1" selection. Chance alignment is more plausible here than for the tightest pairs.
